$comment: C99 6.7.6.2 + 6.7.7p2 (D-CSUBSET-VLA): a POINTER whose pointee comes from a typedef carrying a runtime bound — `typedef int R[n]; R *p = a;` (the alias is the POINTEE) and `typedef int (*P)[n]; P q = a;` (the alias IS the pointer). Both were EXCLUDED by the C4b typedef gate and both are compiled AND RUN by gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 (probed separately, -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra, 2026-09-01), so the reference disjunction requires them. A pointer to a VLA row reserves a fixed 8 bytes, but its SUBSCRIPT steps by the pointee's RUNTIME row size, and that number must be INHERITED from what the typedef froze once (6.7.7p2) rather than re-derived from `n` — re-deriving it is a SILENT miscompile: the program still runs, just through the wrong rows. Witnesses: (A) FREEZE-ONCE THROUGH THE POINTER — `n` is mutated to 100 between the typedef and the pointer, so a re-derived stride would be 400 and every cross-check against the array `a` would miss (returns 1..6); (B) OFF-DIAGONAL BOTH WAYS — p[1][0] vs p[0][2] are distinct cells, written through the pointer and read through the array and back (returns 1..7); (C) THE POINTER-TYPEDEF ARM — `P q = a` must agree cell for cell (returns 8..11); (D) both pointers use the INIT form (`= a`), the spelling D-CSUBSET-VLA-PTR-INIT-FORM-TYPING once deferred, which must keep working through the typedef composition. main is a LEAF (no calls). ⚠ 'The C1b VLA frame-model scope' was leaf-ONLY and that boundary is GONE since 2026-09-04 (P59) — the non-leaf VLA frame model shipped and D-CSUBSET-VLA-NONLEAF-CALL-FRAME is CLOSED; still a leaf, now by CHOICE. `volatile` defeats const-folding so the bound is genuinely runtime. The `release` arm proves the frozen stride slots survive the full optimizer. exitCode 42; returns 1..11 are the strict in-program pins. Red-on-disable: revert the semantic origin gate to `declTy == headTy` and (A)/(B)/(D) stop compiling; drop the Ptr arm from the MIR TypeDecl freeze and (C) stops compiling.
